definitions.explanation: A form of storytelling using illustrated cards that are displayed one at a time in a small wooden stage, while the narrator tells the story.

examples.japanese: {紙芝居|かみしばい}を{読|よ}む。
{図書館|としょかん}で{紙芝居|かみしばい}の{読|よ}み{聞|き}かせがある。
examples.english: There is a kamishibai reading at the library.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{紙芝居|かみしばい}のおじさんが{公園|こうえん}に{来|き}て、{子|こ}どもたちにお{菓子|かし}を{売|う}りながら{物語|ものがたり}を{聞|き}かせてくれた。
examples.english: In the old days, a kamishibai man would come to the park, selling sweets to the children while telling them stories.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTES:
Kamishibai was a popular form of street entertainment in Japan from the 1930s through the 1950s. A performer would travel by bicycle, set up a small wooden stage on the back, and tell stories using illustrated cards. Children would gather to watch, buying candy from the performer. Though street kamishibai has largely disappeared, it is still used in libraries, schools, and kindergartens as an educational tool.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙芝居|かみしばい}を{演|えん}じる: to perform kamishibai
- {紙芝居|かみしばい}を{読|よ}む: to read/narrate kamishibai
- {紙芝居|かみしばい}{屋|や}: kamishibai performer
